conclusion: Both preregistered arms trained but evaluation never produced a scoreboard. Two independent, stacked environment/harness defects blocked scripts/evaluate_model.py's AgentV publish step (src/slm_training/evals/agentv.py): (1) the fresh session checkout had not run `npm ci`, so `node_modules/@agentv/core` was missing and `_agentv_runtime` raised RuntimeError before spawning the node runner; (2) once node_modules is restored, this session's environment injects a NODE_OPTIONS value (`--import tsx`) that the pinned Node build rejects with exit 9, and publish_agentv_evaluation's subprocess.run call inherited the unsanitized environment, so the node runner itself crashed. The first defect (npm ci) was already fixed on origin/main by a concurrent session (commit 3cb0638, PR #1327) together with a stale ship-gate fixture fix; this cycle discovered and fixed the second, still-open defect.
